authority: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618 syllabus, 2027-2029, Version 2

records.resolution: Directly teaches both the need for and purpose of professional ethics, connecting public interest, competence and accountability to computing decisions.
Explains why joining a professional ethical body matters and names BCS and IEEE with their full names, codes, guidance, development and accountability roles.
Requires a scenario-based ethical or unethical judgement and explains stakeholder impacts of both courses of action rather than accepting an unsupported label.
Explains why copyright legislation is needed for easily copied software and distinguishes statutory rights, protected expression and licence permission.
Covers FSF, OSI, shareware and commercial software and requires scenario-linked licence justification across teaching, practice and three assessment forms.
Teaches AI applications and traces social, economic and environmental impacts with benefits, harms, mitigations and contextual evaluation.

Replaces the generic tablet evaluation with an 8-mark AI route-optimisation scenario that directly assesses the application plus all three required impact dimensions without changing question count or marks.

Adds a visible CORE checkpoint to the Section 7 review lesson covering BCS/IEEE, ethical/unethical impacts, copyright need, all four licence examples and AI applications with social, economic and environmental impacts; the existing facial-recognition lesson question is explicitly identified as AI.
